issue: Does a forensic search of a cell phone at the border require reasonable suspicion, as opposed to a manual search that requires no individualized suspicion?

sides.position: A forensic search of a cell phone at the border requires reasonable suspicion (manual searches need none).
cases: United States v. Cano, 934 F.3d 1002 (9th Cir. 2019)

sides.position: A forensic border search of a cell phone does not require reasonable suspicion or other individualized suspicion, as the opposing side of the division.

quote: The circuits are divided over whether reasonable suspicion is required for a forensic search of a cell phone at the border.
cite: United States v. Castillo, 70 F.4th 894 (5th Cir. 2023)
